A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-sample estimation problem for k-SAT-truncated Ising models. Their complete text, equations, algorithms, Figure 1 and appendices A–F support comparison; the appendices match apart from page numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and proofs, including the application in Appendix F. Figure 1 is illustrative; no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its added references and discussion do not introduce original empirical results.

M1.justification: The pseudolikelihood objective, projected-gradient estimator and independent-set construction are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. The revised mathematical bound does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. The added peer-effects motivation does not constitute evaluated domain coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the estimator. Added citations and theoretical comparisons do not introduce experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains an empirical evaluation protocol, and v2 introduces no evaluation settings or testing procedures.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or empirical case studies are added. Appendix F's theoretical application remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The probability guarantees concern theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: No empirical scores, rankings or observed findings are added or revised. Changes to mathematical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.6 replaces min_kappa Pr[σ_j=kappa]/2 with exp(-B)Pr[e_j(σ)=1]/Δ². v2 also adds a lower-bound transfer argument and an Ω(n/Δ²) squared-Frobenius-norm observation. The main theorems and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The new Lower Bounds remark in Section 1.1 claims constant-factor optimality of the clause-size condition for bounded-degree graphs. This extends v1's retained minimax estimation-rate claim; the principal consistency and runtime guarantees are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting connectivity to signal strength and uniform coupling magnitudes to peer influence. It also explains the difficulty of transferring tighter product-distribution lower bounds and revises future directions toward Sherrington–Kirkpatrick models and constrained logistic regression.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Algorithm 1 retain the same inputs, step size, stopping rule and projection procedure. No implementation resources, code/data access information or hardware details are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds three peer-effects references: BLM00, DS03 and Sac01. It also explicitly positions the clause-size guarantee against lower bounds in the already-cited GKK24 and GGZ25; the existing related-work sections remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title now specifies inverse-temperature learning. Targeted introductory rewrites clarify k-SAT terminology and the technical overview, add labeled remarks, and revise the conclusion's future questions. The overall section structure and appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: The longer title occupies two lines, labeled remarks alter the main-text layout, and references now begin on a separate page after the conclusion. Figure 1, its caption and both algorithm displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity through its more precise title, explicit lower-bound comparison and explanations of existing assumptions. Lemma 3.6 now includes degree and flippability dependence present in the appendix argument, although its coefficient still differs by a factor of two from the unchanged Appendix E.3 derivation. These are limited gains in exposition and consistency, without a fully reconciled proof revision.
